name: Nicole Pavlik Law Firm
bio_short: Nicole Pavlik founded Nicole Pavlik Law in 2013 with a clear ambition: to be the kind of estate planning attorney she would want for her own family. Calm in difficult moments, generous with explanations, and deeply prepared for every meeting.
bio_long: Nicole Pavlik founded Nicole Pavlik Law in 2013 with a clear ambition: to be the kind of estate planning attorney she would want for her own family. Calm in difficult moments, generous with explanations, and deeply prepared for every meeting. Her path to the law began as a paralegal, where she watched firsthand how legal work either supports a family or talks past them. She earned her Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice from Arizona State University, then her Juris Doctor from Arizona Summit Law School. She is a member of the State Bar of Arizona and the Probate and Trust Section. Nicole built the firm around proactive planning rather than adversarial practice. The work she does today, helping clients put a thoughtful plan in place, prevents the disputes other lawyers spend their careers untangling. Her firm and team are based in Phoenix, Arizona, while Nicole lives in Maryville, Tennessee. Client meetings are conducted virtually, which keeps her available to Arizona families without the constraints of a single office address.

name: Sobampo Law Firm
bio_short: Mr. Sobampo is the managing director of Sobampo Law Firm, PLLC. Mr. Sobampo was admitted to practice law in March 2010 and since then has concentrated in the areas of immigration and family law. Before admission, attorney Sobampo dedicated over fifteen years to private industry…
bio_long: Mr. Sobampo is the managing director of Sobampo Law Firm, PLLC. Mr. Sobampo was admitted to practice law in March 2010 and since then has concentrated in the areas of immigration and family law. Before admission, attorney Sobampo dedicated over fifteen years to private industry where he owned and managed several multi-million dollar companies. While in law school Mr. Sobampo did an externship working as assistant city prosecutor for the city of Surprise, Arizona. Prior to admission Mr. Sobampo clerked for two years for attorneys practicing in the areas of immigration and family law. Mr. Sobampo has been recognized, among many other things, for his dedication to serving the underserved Latino population in Arizona. He has provided hundreds of volunteer hours to immigration efforts such as the citizenship drives sponsored by Congressman Ed Pastor and with the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance Program sponsored by the IRS, and the Maricopa County Family Lawyer’s Assistance Program. Also, Mr. Sobampo dedicates part of his time to teaching as a part-time faculty at his alma matter and other local colleges and universities in Arizona.
